result.topic_en: Euler states a general problem: find the least exponent x for which f·a^x + g is divisible by a given number N. He solves it by repeatedly adding or subtracting multiples of N to the residue so as to split off powers of a, and suggests shortcuts using squares and cubes of small residues.
result.transcription:
246
Problema generale.
§. 8. Proposita formula $fa^x+g$, inuenire minimum exponentem $x$, quo haec formula per datum numerum N fiat diuisibilis, siquidem id fuerit possibile.
Solutio.
Quaestio ergo huc reducitur, vt forma $fa^x$ per numerum datum N diuisa relinquat residuum $=-g$. Quia nunc per Lemma primum pro residuo etiam haberi potest $-g\mp\lambda N$, facile $\lambda$ ita assumere licebit, vt haec formula factorem obtineat $a$, vel adeo eius altiorem potestatem $a^\alpha$. Sit igitur $-g\mp\lambda N=a^\alpha.r$, atque per lemma postremum quantitas $fa^{x-\alpha}$ per N diuisa residuum relinquet $=r$. Iam simili modo fiat $r\mp\lambda N=a^\beta.s$, et quantitas $fa^{x-\alpha-\beta}$ dabit residuum $s$, sicque vlterius progredi licebit, sumendo $s\mp\lambda N=a^\gamma.t$; tum vero etiam $t\mp\lambda N=a^\delta.u$; porro $u\mp\lambda.N=a^\epsilon.v$ etc.; quo pacto quantitas $a^{x-\alpha-\beta-\gamma-\delta-\epsilon}$ per N diuisa residuum relinquet $=v$; haeque operationes eousque continuentur, donec perueniatur ad residuum $=f$; ita, vt haec quantitas $fa^{x-\alpha-\beta-\gamma\text{ etc.}}$ residuum det $=f$; id quod semper continget, siquidem quaestio fuerit possibilis; atque hoc adeo antequam numeri ab exponente subtrahendi $\alpha+\beta+\gamma+\delta+\epsilon$ etc. superent numerum $N-1$, quia si exponentes ipsius $a$ vltra hunc limitem continuentur, eadem residua recurrunt. Cum autem ad talem casum fuerit peruentum, quo residuum est $f$, quia hoc euenit, si exponens ipsius $a$ fuerit $=0$; hinc concludemus $x=\alpha+\beta+\gamma+\delta$ etc. Omnes ergo has operationes ita succincte repraesentasse iuuabit:

247
$-g\mp\lambda.N=a^\alpha.r$
$r\mp\lambda.N=a^\beta.s$
$s\mp\lambda.N=a^\gamma.t$
$t\mp\lambda.N=a^\delta.u$
$\cdots\cdots$
$\cdots\cdots$
$z\mp\lambda.N=a^\zeta.f$
hincque deducitur conclusio $x=\alpha+\beta+\gamma+\delta\ldots+\zeta$. Sin autem nunquam perueniatur ad tale residuum $f$, antequam summa $\alpha+\beta+\gamma+\delta\ldots$ vsque ad $N-1$ ascendat, problema pro impossibili est habendum.
Quanquam hae operationes expedite instituuntur; tamen eas saepenumero haud mediocriter contrahere licebit, praecipue si peruentum fuerit ad exiguum residuum, puta $t$, respondens formulae $fa^{x-\vartheta}$, ponendo $\vartheta=\alpha+\beta+\gamma$; tum enim eius quadratum $tt$ respondebit formulae $ff.a^{2x-2\vartheta}$, quae per primam diuidatur, vt formulae $fa^{x-2\vartheta}$ respondeat residuo $\frac{tt}{-g}$; quod si non fuerit numerus integer, loco $tt$ scribendo $tt\mp\lambda N$, facile eo reducitur. Quin etiam cubus residui $t^3$ respondebit formulae $f^3a^{3x-3\vartheta}$, quae per quadratum primae diuisa dabit formulae $fa^{x-3\vartheta}$ residuum $=\frac{t^3}{gg}$. Quin etiam binas formulas diuersas in se inuicem ducere licebit, et per primam diuidendo iterum ad nouam huiusmodi formulam peruenietur. Inprimis autem hoc compendium maximum vsum praestabit, vbi ad residua satis parua fuerit peruentum; quorum potestates etiam superio-
res

items.quote: Proposita formula $fa^x+g$, inuenire minimum exponentem $x$, quo haec formula per datum numerum N fiat diuisibilis, siquidem id fuerit possibile.
items.english: Given the formula f·a^x + g, find the least exponent x for which this formula becomes divisible by a given number N, provided this is possible.

items.quote: Sin autem nunquam perueniatur ad tale residuum $f$, antequam summa $\alpha+\beta+\gamma+\delta\ldots$ vsque ad $N-1$ ascendat, problema pro impossibili est habendum.
items.english: But if one never reaches such a residue f before the sum α+β+γ+δ… rises to N−1, the problem must be regarded as impossible.

items.quote: quia si exponentes ipsius $a$ vltra hunc limitem continuentur, eadem residua recurrunt.
items.english: because if the exponents of a are continued beyond this limit, the same residues recur.
